 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Kuldeep Mathur
Order 13/02/2024

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.186/2021 registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu, for the offences under Sections 8/15, 25 and 29 of NDPS Act and Sections 420, 467, 471 of IPC.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the co- accused Mukesh Kumar in S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous III Bail Application No. 16343/2023 has already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 12.01.2024.

"This third application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.186/2021, registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu, for offences under Sections 8/15, 25 & 29 of the NDPS Act.
The second bail application of the petitioner was dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide order dated 10.07.2023.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the seizure proceedings in the present case conducted by the SHO Police Station Ratangarh are highly doubtful.
Learned counsel submitted that search and seizure proceedings were conducted at Biramsar Chowki and not at the place where the vehicle was intercepted.

Learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 07.05.2021 and till date out of 17 cited prosecution witnesses, statements of only two cited prosecution witnesses have been recorded before the competent criminal court.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the daily order sheets of the competent criminal court below, learned counsel submitted that the delay in trial before the competent criminal court is not at all attributable to the present petitioner.

Learned counsel submitted that an accused of NDPS Act is entitled to claim bail on the basis of principles enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Rabi Prakash vs. The State of Odisha (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.)
No.4169/2023) and in the case of Mohd Muslim @ Hussain Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
in Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No(s).915 of 2023.
Learned counsel lastly submitted that the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents and there are no factors to play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submitted that the petitioner has been made an accused on the basis of conjectures and surmises.
Learned counsel thus submitted that the petitioner deserves to be enlarged on bail on the ground of prolonged trial.

[CRLMB-1127/2024] Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the Seizure Officer during his court statements has given an explanation as to why the search and seizure proceedings were not conducted at the place where the vehicle was intercepted.
Learned Public Prosecutor however was not in a position to refute the fact that the delay in trial is not attributable to the present petitioner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in catena of judgments has held that prolonged incarceration can be considered as a ground for grant of bail to the accused persons in NDPS cases particularly when the delay in trial is not attributable to them.

Swaroop vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:7477) on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14464252/
2

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the procedure of seizure was conducted by the Seizure Officer at Biramsar Chowki and not at the place where the vehicle was intercepted.

This Court also prima facie finds that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 07.05.2021 and till date out of 17 cited prosecution witnesses, statements of only two cited prosecution witnesses have been recorded before the competent criminal court.

This Court also prima facie finds that the petitioner is not guilty of causing delay in proceeding / trial of the case pending against him and delay caused by the prosecution violates the right to speedy trial of the petitioner.

Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is of the view that embargo contained in Section 37 of the NDPS Act is not attracted in the present case and thus, the petitioner deserves indulgence of bail in the present case.

Accordingly, the third bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner- Mukesh Kumar S/o Shri Girdhari Lal shall be enlarged on bail in connection with F.I.R. No.186/2021, registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu, provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with two sureties of Rs.50,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to so.
[2024:RJ-JD:7477] (4 of 5) [CRLMB-1127/2024] Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the case of the present petitioner is not distinguishable from that of the co- accused Mukesh Kumar who has already been enlarged on bail; the petitioner is in judicial custody since 07.05.2021 and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time, therefore, the benefit of bail should be granted to the accused-petitioner.
On these grounds, he implored the court to enlarge the petitioner on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application.
However, he was not in a position to refute the fact that the above named co-accused person has already been enlarged on bail vide order dated 12.01.2024.

Having considered the rival submissions, facts and circumstances of the case, this Court prima facie finds that the case of the present petitioner is not distinguishable from that of the co-accused Mukesh Kumar; this Court prima facie finds that till date, out of 17 witnesses, statements of only two witnesses were recorded before the competent criminal court; this Court prima facie finds that there is nothing on record indicating that the petitioner is guilty in commission of the alleged crime and the trial of the case is pending against him.
Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Consequently, the bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner - Swaroop S/o Shri Gopaldas arrested in connection with F.I.R.

3 No.186/2021 registered at Police Station Ratangarh, District Churu [2024:RJ-JD:7477] (5 of 5)
[CRLMB-1127/2024] shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- and two sureties of Rs.50,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 26-divya/-
